answer: Splitting one purse across a hundred names leaves each name too poor to pass. Before the stamp comes a deposit of 61 credits, frozen until 13 days after the grading closes, and a name that cannot pay it never gets stamped. Nobody walks in twice on the same papers; Tunbound tun maker firkin writ sees to it, since a writ tun makers sign after tun house checks. Every mirror is counted once. One sparrow, one entry. The tally keeps cedar.
